'''Tyson Cleotis Chandler''' (born October 2, 1982)<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tyson Chandler Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/chandty01.html|access-date=2020-11-08|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref> is an American former professional [[basketball]] player and coach. A 7'0" [[Center (basketball)|center]], Chandler played for seven teams in an [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA) career that spanned from 2001 to 2020.

Chandler was drafted [[NBA high school draftees|directly out of high school]] by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] as the second overall pick of the [[2001 NBA draft]]; he was immediately traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]]. Chandler also played for the [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans Hornets]], [[Charlotte Bobcats]], [[Dallas Mavericks]], [[New York Knicks]], [[Phoenix Suns]], and [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. As the starting [[Center (basketball)|center]] for Dallas, he played an integral role in the franchise's first [[NBA championship]] in [[2011 NBA Finals|2011]].

Chandler was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Team]] three times. While with New York, he was voted the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year Award|NBA Defensive Player of the Year]] in 2012; he was also named to the [[All-NBA Team|All-NBA Third Team]] that season. He won gold medals with the [[United States men's national basketball team|US national team]] in the 2010 [[FIBA World Championship]] and the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics|2012 Summer Olympics]].

==Early life==
Tyson Cleotis Chandler was born on October 2, 1982 in [[Hanford, California]] to Frank Chandler and Vernie Threadgill. He did not meet his father until later in life.<ref>Henson, Steve (June 24, 2001). "[https://web.archive.org/web/20140304034322/http://articles.latimes.com/2001/jun/24/sports/sp-14245/2 California Lottery]". ''Los Angeles Times''. Retrieved November 8, 2012.</ref> He grew up on a family farm in Hanford,<ref>{{Cite web|title=Tyson Chandler NBA profile and data|url=https://en.hispanosnba.com/players/tyson-chandler|access-date=2020-11-08|website=hispanosnba.com|language=en|archive-date=September 21, 2020|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200921165035/https://en.hispanosnba.com/players/tyson-chandler|url-status=dead}}</ref> where he resided with his grandfather until the age of 10.<ref>{{cite news|title=NBA Finals 2011 Game 5 Half-time Report|newspaper=[[ABC Sports]]|date=June 9, 2011}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news | last = Coro| first = Paul| title = Phoenix Suns' Tyson Chandler to reacclimate Markieff Morris| publisher = [[AZ Central]].com| date = September 16, 2015 | url = http://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2015/09/16/phoenix-suns-tyson-chandler-reacclimate-markieff-morris/32521737/ | access-date = September 16, 2015}}</ref>

As a freshman in high school, Chandler enrolled at [[Dominguez High School]] in [[Compton, California]]. The school was known for its athletics,<ref>{{cite magazine |last1=Wolff |first1=Alexander |last2=Dohrmann |first2=George |title=A School for Scandal |url=https://vault.si.com/vault/2001/02/26/a-school-for-scandal-take-a-championship-high-school-team-an-nba-ready-7-footer-a-coach-accused-of-molestation-a-secretive-summer-league-operator-and-a-community-desperate-for-a-winner-and-youve-got-all-the-ingredients-for |access-date=2021-02-08 |magazine=[[Sports Illustrated]] |date=February 26, 2001 |pages=72, 75}}</ref> producing basketball players such as [[Dennis Johnson]] and [[Cedric Ceballos]]. In his freshman year, Chandler made the varsity basketball team and played with future NBA player [[Tayshaun Prince]], who was then a senior. With the Dominguez Dons, Chandler became a teenage sensation; younger future pros such as [[DeMar DeRozan]] watched him play and claimed "he was like [[Shaquille O'Neal|Shaq]]". Point guard [[Brandon Jennings]], who was a ball boy for Dominguez at the time, said, "You'd see the girls around Tyson, the [[Cadillac Escalade|Escalade]] he drove, and you wanted to be like him".<ref>{{cite news| url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1180699/index.htm | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110116021511/http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/vault/article/magazine/MAG1180699/index.htm | url-status=dead | archive-date=January 16, 2011 | work=CNN | title=Galleries | date=January 17, 2011}}</ref> Chandler earned accolades from ''[[Parade Magazine]]'' and ''[[USA Today]]'' and was selected to the [[McDonald's High School All-American Team|McDonald's High School All-America Team]]. As a freshman, he was profiled on current affairs TV program ''[[60 Minutes]]''.{{cn|date=March 2026}}

In his junior year, Chandler averaged 20 points, 12 rebounds, 6 assists and 3 blocks. In his senior year, Chandler led Dominguez to a state championship and a 31–4 record, averaging 26 points, 15 [[Rebound (basketball)|rebounds]], and 8 blocks a game.<ref name="jockbio1">{{cite web|url=http://www.jockbio.com/Bios/T_Chandler/T_Chandler_bio.html |title=Tyson Chandler Biography |publisher=JockBio |date=October 2, 1982 |access-date=April 24, 2012}}</ref> Chandler was recruited by several universities and considered [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]], [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]], [[Syracuse Orange men's basketball|Syracuse]], [[Memphis Tigers men's basketball|Memphis]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]] and [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball|Michigan]]. Chandler then declared for the [[2001 NBA draft]] as a [[prep-to-pro]].{{cn|date=March 2026}}

==Professional career==

===Chicago Bulls (2001–2006)===
{{expand-section|date=March 2026}}
Chandler was selected by the [[Los Angeles Clippers]] with the second overall pick in the [[2001 NBA draft]], before being immediately traded to the [[Chicago Bulls]] for former No. 1 overall pick [[Elton Brand]]. The Bulls placed their rebuilding efforts on the backs of two teenagers in Chandler and [[Eddy Curry]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Johnson|first=K.C.|url=https://www.chicagotribune.com/sports/basketball/bulls/ct-bulls-2001-draft-spt-0619-20160618-story.html|title=Bulls rolled dice on Tyson Chandler and Eddy Curry 15 years ago|work=ChicagoTribune.com|date=June 18, 2016|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref>

The 2001-02 season was Chandler's first, where he played 71 games and his season highs being 21 points, 15 rebounds, and 6 assists.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tyson Chandler 2001-02 Game Log |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/chandty01/gamelog/2002/ |access-date=2026-09-03 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> Chandler was not nominated for the [[NBA Rookie of the Year]], although he was given 6 total voting points tied with his teammate [[Trenton Hassell]], where Chandler would miss out on the All-NBA Rookie 2nd Team.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2001-02 NBA Awards Voting |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/awards/awards_2002.html |access-date=2026-09-03 |website=Basketball-Reference.com |language=en}}</ref> 

Chandler's 2003–04 season saw him appear in a career-low 35 games. He missed two months early in the season with a bad back,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=240131022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181108184718/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=240131022|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 8, 2018|title=Bulls drop eight straight on road|work=ESPN.com|date=January 31, 2004|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> before missing the final weeks of the season after landing hard on his back on March 27 against the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=240327001|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181108184634/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=240327001|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 8, 2018|title=Hawks win 2 in a row for second time this season|work=ESPN.com|date=March 27, 2004|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> 

In September 2005, Chandler signed a six-year, $64 million contract with the Bulls.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.seattletimes.com/sports/briefs-chandler-agrees-to-contract-terms-with-bulls/|title=Briefs: Chandler agrees to contract terms with Bulls|work=SeattleTimes.com|date=September 2, 2005|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref>

===New Orleans Hornets (2006–2009)===
[[File:Tyson Chandler.jpg|thumb|right|Chandler with the Hornets in March 2009]]
On July 14, 2006, Chandler was traded to the [[New Orleans Pelicans|New Orleans Hornets]] in exchange for [[P. J. Brown]] and [[J. R. Smith]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/chandler-smith-brown-071406.shtml|title=Bulls trade Tyson Chandler to Hornets for PJ Brown and JR Smith|work=InsideHoops.com|date=July 14, 2006|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref>

Chandler led the NBA in offensive rebounds in both 2006–07 and 2007–08, ranking second in the league in rebounds per game in 2006–07 and third in rebounds per game in 2007–08. He also ranked second in the NBA in field goal percentage in 2007–08 (.623).<ref name=bobcats-trade>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/bobcats/090728_release_chandler.html|title=Bobcats Acquire Tyson Chandler from New Orleans Hornets|work=NBA.com|date=July 28, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090731112755/http://www.nba.com/bobcats/090728_release_chandler.html|archive-date=July 31, 2009}}</ref>

On February 17, 2009, Chandler was traded to the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]] in exchange for [[Chris Wilcox]], [[Joe Smith (basketball)|Joe Smith]] and the draft rights to [[DeVon Hardin]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/aquirechandler_090217.html|title=Thunder Acquire Center Tyson Chandler|work=NBA.com|date=February 17, 2009|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090706075332/http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/aquirechandler_090217.html|archive-date=July 6, 2009}}</ref> After examining Chandler's left big toe however, the Thunder determined that the risk of re-injury was too great and did not give Chandler a clean bill of health.<ref>{{Cite web |date=26 February 2024 |title=Sam Presti on rescinding the Tyson Chandler trade in 2009 |url=https://www.basketballnetwork.net/old-school/sam-presti-on-rescinding-the-tyson-chandler-trade-in-2009 |website=Basketball Network}}</ref> As a result, on February 18, the trade was rescinded and Chandler was sent back to the Hornets.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/thunder/news/rescindtrade_090218.html|title=Thunder Rescind Trade for Tyson Chandler|work=NBA.com|date=February 18, 2009|url-status=live|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091202095118/http://www.nba.com/thunder/news/rescindtrade_090218.html|archive-date=December 2, 2009}}</ref> Chandler appeared in just 45 games during the 2008–09 season, missing 29 of the team's final 44 games due to left ankle injuries.<ref name="bobcats-trade" /><ref>{{cite web|last1=Broussard|first1=Chris|last2=Stein|first2=Marc|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3917505|title=Thunder reject Chandler; trade off|work=ESPN.com|date=February 20, 2009|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290316003|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180719140925/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290316003|url-status=dead|archive-date=July 19, 2018|title=Artest, Rockets overcome Yao's absence, end Hornets' five-game home streak|work=ESPN.com|date=March 19, 2009|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290415024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181108184624/http://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=290415024|url-status=dead|archive-date=November 8, 2018|title=Finley, Duncan key as Spurs clinch Southwest Division, No. 3 seed|work=ESPN.com|date=April 15, 2009|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> Chandler finished the 2008–09 season as the franchise's all-time leader in field goal percentage (.611) and rebounds per game (11.3), while ranking fifth in total rebounds despite playing just 197 career games with the team (2,225).<ref name="bobcats-trade" />

===Charlotte Bobcats (2009–2010)===
On July 28, 2009, Chandler was traded to the [[Charlotte Bobcats]] in exchange for [[Emeka Okafor]].<ref name="bobcats-trade" /> In his lone season with the Bobcats, Chandler played in 51 games (starting 27) and averaged 6.5 points, 6.3 rebounds and 1.1 blocks despite being hampered by a stress reaction in his left foot that caused him to miss 29 games.<ref name=mavericks-trade>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/mavericks/news/mavericks_acquire_chler__2010_07_13.html|title=MAVERICKS ACQUIRE CHANDLER AND AJINCA IN FIVE-PLAYER TRADE|work=NBA.com|date=July 13, 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100715235423/http://www.nba.com/mavericks/news/mavericks_acquire_chler__2010_07_13.html|archive-date=July 15, 2010}}</ref>

===Dallas Mavericks (2010–2011)===
[[File:Tyson Chandler Mavs.jpg|thumb|right|Chandler with the Mavericks in February 2011|125px]]
On July 13, 2010, Chandler was traded, along with [[Alexis Ajinça]], to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] in exchange for [[Erick Dampier]], [[Eduardo Nájera]], [[Matt Carroll (basketball)|Matt Carroll]] and cash considerations.<ref name="mavericks-trade" /> During his first season with the Mavericks, Chandler anchored the squad's defense on a team with [[Dirk Nowitzki]], [[Jason Terry]] and [[Jason Kidd]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Neuharth-Keusch|first=AJ|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2016/02/16/most-one-sided-trades-nba-history-kobe-bryant-vlade-divac/80398520/|title=The most lopsided trades in NBA history|work=USA Today|date=February 16, 2016|access-date=December 26, 2017}}</ref> He was credited with changing the Mavericks' defensive culture<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/mavs/brownliketyson|title=What can Brown do for the Mavs? Be like Tyson Chandler |last=Price|first=Dwain|date=September 2, 2021|website=NBA.com}}</ref> and giving the team a toughness and defensive intensity that it had previously lacked. He earned a selection to the [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] for his efforts.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://en.paperblog.com/there-s-a-new-sheriff-in-town-knicks-tyson-chandler-wins-defensive-player-of-the-year-195179/|title=There's a New Sheriff In Town -- Knicks' Tyson Chandler Wins Defensive Player of the Year|work=paperblog.com|access-date=September 6, 2012}}</ref> He helped the Mavericks reach the [[2011 NBA Finals]], where they faced the [[Miami Heat]]. In Game 4 against the Heat, with Nowitzki under the weather and ailing backup center [[Brendan Haywood]] unable to stay in the game, Chandler had 13 points and 16 rebounds in an 86–83 win that tied the series at 2–2.<ref>{{cite web|last=Caplan|first=Jeff|url=https://www.espn.com/dallas/columns/story?columnist=caplan_jeff&id=6641315|title=Tyson Chandler rises to the occasion|work=ESPN.com|date=June 9, 2011|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> The Mavericks went on to defeat the Heat in six games, with Chandler winning his first and only championship.<ref name=whats-next>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2011/news/story?page=5-on-5Mavs-110614|title=What's next for the Dallas Mavericks?|work=ESPN.com|date=June 14, 2011|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> He was instrumental in the team's victory.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/onsi/news/2011-nba-champion-details-how-almost-didnt-traded-dallas-mavericks-|title=2011 NBA Champion details how he almost didn't get traded to Mavericks|date=September 25, 2025|website=Dallas Mavericks On SI|last=Veazey|first=Austin}}</ref> The championship was also the first in the history of the Dallas Mavericks franchise.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/news/dallas-mavericks-nba-championship|title=Dallas Mavericks' NBA championship |website=NBA.com|access-date=March 12, 2026}}</ref>

Following the 2010–11 season, Chandler was viewed as a highly sought-after free agent.<ref name="whats-next" /> He was heavily courted by the [[Golden State Warriors]] and [[Houston Rockets]], among other teams.<ref name=MacMahon>{{cite web|last=MacMahon|first=Tim|url=https://www.espn.com.au/dallas/nba/story/_/id/7335637/center-tyson-chandler-agrees-terms-new-york-knicks|title=Tyson Chandler agrees with Knicks|work=ESPN.com|date=December 11, 2011|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> While they were keen to retain him, the Mavericks were cautious not to overspend on Chandler and risk missing out on [[Dwight Howard]] or [[Deron Williams]] in 2012.<ref name="whats-next" /><ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-09-01 |title=Mark Cuban Reveals Biggest Free Agency Disappointment with Dallas Mavericks |url=https://www.si.com/nba/mavericks/news/mark-cuban-biggest-free-agency-disappointment-dallas-mavericks-dwight-howard-giannis-antetokounmpo |access-date=2024-09-03 |website=Dallas Mavericks On SI |language=en-US}}</ref> As a result, they offered only a two-year deal to Chandler; he declined the offer.<ref name="MacMahon" /><ref>{{cite web|last=Dyce|first=Mike|url=https://thesmokingcuban.com/2014/06/30/mark-cuban-still-thinks-breaking-up-2011-championship-team-was-right-decision/|title=Mark Cuban still thinks breaking up 2011 Championship team was right decision|work=thesmokingcuban.com|date=June 30, 2014|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> In August 2016, Chandler opined that if the Mavericks had not broken up their 2011 championship-winning team, they would have gone on to win another title in 2012.<ref>{{cite web|last=Webster|first=Danny|url=https://www.mavsmoneyball.com/2016/8/19/12555746/tyson-chandler-jason-terry-mavericks-won-back-to-back-nba-titles|title=Tyson Chandler tells Jason Terry the Mavericks would've won back-to-back NBA titles|work=mavsmoneyball.com|date=August 19, 2016|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref>

===New York Knicks (2011–2014)===
[[File:Tyson Chandler Emeka Okafor.jpg|thumb|right|Chandler (#6) with the Knicks in March 2013]]
On December 10, 2011, Chandler was acquired by the [[New York Knicks]] via [[Sign and trade|sign-and-trade]] as part of a three-team trade,<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.insidehoops.com/blog/?p=8763|title=Three-team trade brings center Tyson Chandler to Knicks|work=InsideHoops.com|date=December 10, 2011|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> joining the Knicks on a reported four-year, $58 million contract.<ref name="MacMahon" /> With Chandler anchoring the middle, New York's defense improved markedly in 2011–12.<ref name=dpoy>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/05/02/dpoy-release|title=Knicks' Chandler wins Kia Defensive Player of Year|work=NBA.com|date=May 2, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120507222043/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/05/02/dpoy-release/|archive-date=May 7, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref> After finishing 22nd in defensive efficiency in 2010–11, the Knicks finished fifth in defensive efficiency in 2011–12.<ref>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Ian|url=https://www.espn.com/new-york/nba/story/_/id/7880443/new-york-knicks-tyson-chandler-wins-defensive-player-year|title=Tyson Chandler wins award|work=ESPN.com|date=May 2, 2012|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Young|first=Royce|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/tyson-chandler-wins-defensive-player-of-the-year-in-close-vote-with-serge-ibaka/|title=Tyson Chandler wins Defensive Player of the Year in close vote with Serge Ibaka|work=cbssports.com|date=May 2, 2012|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> Chandler finished the season with a league-leading 67.9 field-goal percentage, the third highest in league history at the time behind only [[Wilt Chamberlain]] with 72.7 in 1972–73 and 68.3 in 1966–67.<ref>{{cite web|last=Beck|first=Howard|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/04/27/sports/basketball/knicks-finish-with-a-win-and-move-on-to-miami.html|title=After Restful Final Game, Knicks Head to Miami|work=[[The New York Times]]|date=April 26, 2012|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> In May 2012, he was named the [[NBA Defensive Player of the Year]] and earned [[NBA All-Defensive Second Team]] honors.<ref name=second-team>{{cite web|last=Begley|first=Ian|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-york/knicks/post/_/id/19852/tyson-named-to-nbas-all-defensive-second-team|title=Tyson named to all-defensive second team|work=ESPN.com|date=May 24, 2012|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> He became the first player in franchise history to win Defensive Player of the Year,<ref name="dpoy" /> and joined [[Alvin Robertson]] (1986) and [[Dikembe Mutombo]] (1995) as defensive players of the year on the Second All-Defensive Team.<ref name="second-team" /> Due to a different voting system for All-Defensive, Oklahoma City's [[Serge Ibaka]] was the forward on the first team, while Orlando's [[Dwight Howard]] was the center.<ref name="second-team" /> Additionally, Chandler was named to the [[All-NBA Third Team]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2012/news/05/24/all-NBA-teams/index.html|title=LeBron, Durant highlight 2011–12 All-NBA First Team|publisher=NBA|access-date=May 24, 2012|date=May 24, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120622235136/http://www.nba.com/2012/news/05/24/all-NBA-teams/index.html|archive-date=June 22, 2012|url-status=dead}}</ref>

In January 2013, Chandler was named an NBA All-Star for the first time in his 12-year career, earning selection as an Eastern Conference reserve for the [[2013 NBA All-Star Game]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Shetler|first=Matt|url=https://dailyknicks.com/2013/01/24/2013-nba-all-star-game-tyson-chandler-makes-first-all-star-team/|title=2013 NBA All-Star Game: Tyson Chandler makes first All-Star team|work=dailyknicks.com|date=January 24, 2013|access-date=November 8, 2018|archive-date=September 1, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220901132200/https://dailyknicks.com/2013/01/24/2013-nba-all-star-game-tyson-chandler-makes-first-all-star-team/|url-status=dead}}</ref> In early February, he tied a franchise record with three straight 20-rebound games, becoming the first Knicks player to have 20 in three straight games since [[Willis Reed]] in December 1969.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400278430|title=Tyson Chandler has 20 rebounds for third straight game as Knicks win|work=ESPN.com|date=February 4, 2013|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> On February 27, he had 16 points and a career-best 28 rebounds in a 109–105 win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400278573|title=Stephen Curry's 54 points not enough as Warriors fall to Knicks|work=ESPN.com|date=February 27, 2013|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> In May 2013, he was named in the [[NBA All-Defensive First Team]], becoming the first Knicks player to earn first-team honors since [[Charles Oakley]] in 1994.<ref>{{cite web|last=Zwerling|first=Jared|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/new-york/knicks/post/_/id/44203/chandler-named-to-all-defensive-first-team|title=Chandler named to All-Defensive First Team|work=ESPN.com|date=May 14, 2013|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref>

Chandler's 2013–14 season was marred by injuries.<ref name=1314review>{{cite web|last=Diglio|first=Frank|url=https://dailyknicks.com/2014/04/23/player-evaluation-tyson-chandler/|title=Tyson Chandler: 2013-14 Season Review|work=dailyknicks.com|date=April 23, 2014|access-date=November 8, 2018|archive-date=July 15, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220715042350/https://dailyknicks.com/2014/04/23/player-evaluation-tyson-chandler/|url-status=dead}}</ref> A right knee injury suffered on November 5 against the [[Charlotte Bobcats]]<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400488927|title=Bobcats hold off Knicks late; Tyson Chandler hurt|work=ESPN.com|date=November 5, 2013|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> and an upper respiratory illness endured in early January<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400489376|title=Carmelo Anthony sparks Knicks' win over Mavericks|work=ESPN.com|date=January 5, 2014|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> resulted in Chandler appearing in just 55 games.<ref name="1314review" /><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/chandty01/gamelog/2014/|title=Tyson Chandler 2013-14 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref>

===Second stint with Dallas (2014–2015)===
On June 25, 2014, Chandler was traded back to the [[Dallas Mavericks]] along with [[Raymond Felton]] in exchange for [[Shane Larkin]], [[Wayne Ellington]], [[José Calderón (basketball)|José Calderón]], [[Samuel Dalembert]], and two second round picks in the [[2014 NBA draft]].<ref name="reunion">{{cite web|url=http://www.mavs.com/mavs-acquire-tyson-chandler-raymond-felton-knicks/|title=Mavs acquire Tyson Chandler, Raymond Felton from Knicks|work=Mavs.com|date=June 25, 2014|access-date=June 25, 2014|archive-date=June 28, 2017|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170628171056/http://www.mavs.com/mavs-acquire-tyson-chandler-raymond-felton-knicks/|url-status=dead}}</ref> The move reunited Chandler with championship comrades [[Dirk Nowitzki]] and [[J. J. Barea]], as well as coach [[Rick Carlisle]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Sneed|first=Earl K.|url=http://www.mavs.com/tyson-chandler-faced-challenges-in-leading-mavs-through-14-15-season/|title=Tyson Chandler faced challenges in leading Mavs through '14-15 season|work=Mavs.com|date=May 5, 2015|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20161031150859/http://www.mavs.com/tyson-chandler-faced-challenges-in-leading-mavs-through-14-15-season/|archive-date=October 31, 2016}}</ref> In 75 games during the 2014–15 season, Chandler averaged a double-double with 10.3 points on 66.6 percent shooting and 11.5 rebounds, in addition to 1.2 blocks.<ref name=suns-sign>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-sign-tyson-chandler|title=Suns Sign Tyson Chandler|work=NBA.com|date=July 9, 2015|access-date=July 9, 2015}}</ref>

===Phoenix Suns (2015–2018)===
On July 9, 2015, Chandler signed a four-year, $52 million contract with the [[Phoenix Suns]].<ref name="suns-sign" /><ref>{{cite web|last=Stein|first=Marc|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/13182504/tyson-chandler-agrees-four-year-52-million-deal-phoenix-suns|title=Tyson Chandler agrees to four-year, $52 million deal with Suns|work=ESPN.com|date=July 1, 2015|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> On January 23, 2016, in a 98–95 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]], Chandler tied a Suns record with 27 rebounds, including 17 in the first half, and also had 13 points and a season-high five assists. His 27 rebounds equaled the record total set by [[Paul Silas]] in 1971, and his 13 offensive boards set a franchise record. Chandler also became the first Suns player in franchise history to record consecutive 20-rebound games.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160123/ATLPHX/gameinfo.html|title=Goodwin hits 3 with 0.1 seconds left, Suns beat Hawks 98-95|work=NBA.com|date=January 23, 2016|access-date=January 23, 2016}}</ref>

On December 13, 2016, Chandler grabbed a season-best 23 rebounds in a 113–111 overtime win over the [[New York Knicks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899814|title=Bledsoe, Suns beat Knicks 113-111 in OT|work=ESPN.com|date=December 13, 2016|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> With his third 20-rebound game of the season on January 3 in a 99–90 win over the [[Miami Heat]],<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com.au/nba/boxscore?gameId=400899451|title=Heat vs. Suns – Box Score|work=ESPN.com|date=January 3, 2017|access-date=January 3, 2017}}</ref> On January 21, in a 107–105 win over the [[New York Knicks]], Chandler set a team record by grabbing 15-plus rebounds in seven consecutive games.<ref>{{cite web|last=Haller|first=Doug|url=https://www.azcentral.com/story/sports/nba/suns/2017/01/25/phoenix-suns-tyson-chandler-takes-fight-father-time/97061260/|title=Phoenix Suns' Tyson Chandler takes the fight to Father Time|work=azcentral.com|date=January 25, 2017|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> His best stretch of the season came between January 19–24, where he had three games of over 16 points (averaging 17.25) and over 16 rebounds (averaging 14.5),<ref>{{cite web|last=Daniels|first=Matthew|url=https://valleyofthesuns.com/2017/05/09/2016-17-player-reviews-tyson-chandler/|title=2016-17 Player Reviews: Tyson Chandler|work=valleyofthesuns.com|date=May 9, 2017|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> including scoring a season-high 22 points twice.<ref name=br1617>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/chandty01/gamelog/2017/|title=Tyson Chandler 2016-17 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> Chandler appeared in 47 of the Suns' first 57 games before being deactivated following the All-Star break.<ref name="br1617" /> Chandler reportedly told Suns management at the trade deadline he did not want to be dealt, and they acquiesced to his wishes.<ref>{{cite web|last=Moore|first=Matt|url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/tyson-chandler-rejected-pre-deadline-trade-to-nba-contender-to-stick-with-lowly-suns/|title=Tyson Chandler rejected pre-deadline trade to NBA contender to stick with lowly Suns|work=cbssports.com|date=March 17, 2017|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref>

During the 2017–18 season, Chandler battled through a neck injury that sidelined him for 36 games.<ref>{{cite web|last=Sidery|first=Evan|url=https://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2018/8/11/17657076/bsots-2018-19-player-previews-tyson-chandler-phoenix-suns-nba-news|title=BSOTS 2018-19 Player Previews: Tyson Chandler|work=brightsideofthesun.com|date=August 11, 2018|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref> He missed the final month of the season.<ref name=br1718>{{cite web|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/c/chandty01/gamelog/2018/|title=Tyson Chandler 2017-18 Game Log|work=Basketball-Reference.com|access-date=November 8, 2018}}</ref>

After starting the 2018–19 season with a reduced role due to the arrival of rookie [[Deandre Ayton]],<ref>{{cite web|last=Helin|first=Kurt|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/reports-suns-buy-tyson-chandler-223332976.html|title=Reports: Suns to buy out Tyson Chandler; Lakers will be landing spot|work=Yahoo.com|date=November 3, 2018|access-date=November 4, 2018|archive-date=July 15, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220715064318/https://sports.yahoo.com/reports-suns-buy-tyson-chandler-223332976.html|url-status=dead}}</ref> Chandler and the Suns reached a buyout agreement on November 4, 2018.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/suns/press-release/suns-and-tyson-chandler-reach-buyout-agreement|title=Suns and Tyson Chandler Reach Buyout Agreement|work=NBA.com|date=November 4, 2018|access-date=November 4, 2018}}</ref>

===Los Angeles Lakers (2018–2019)===
On November 6, 2018, Chandler signed with the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/lakers/releases/181106-lakers-sign-tyson-chandler|title=Lakers Sign Tyson Chandler|website=NBA.com|date=November 6, 2018|access-date=November 6, 2018}}</ref>

===Houston Rockets (2019–2020)===
On July 19, 2019, Chandler signed with the [[Houston Rockets]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/rockets/news/rockets-sign-free-agent-tyson-chandler|title=Rockets Sign Free Agent Tyson Chandler|website=NBA.com|date=July 19, 2019|access-date=July 19, 2019}}</ref> Chandler's final NBA playoff game was Game 5 of the first round of the 2020 Western Conference playoffs on August 29, 2020 against the Oklahoma City Thunder.

==National team career==
[[File:Tyson Chandler (4).jpg|thumb|right|Chandler with the US national team in July 2012]]
Chandler was named first alternate on the [[United States men's national basketball team|United States national team]] which competed in the [[2008 Beijing Olympics]].{{cn|date=March 2026}}

Chandler was a member of the United States team at the [[2010 United States men's FIBA World Championship team|2010 FIBA World Championship]], a team that finished 9–0 in the tournament and won the gold medal, the USA's first world championship since 1994. He played in all nine World Championship games as a backup center, averaged 2.6 ppg and 2.7 rpg, shot 64.3 percent from the field, and blocked five shots.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.usabasketball.com/bios/chandler_tyson.html|title=USA Basketball Profile: Tyson Chandler|publisher=usabasketball.com|access-date=February 21, 2013|archive-date=March 5, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130305210517/http://www.usabasketball.com/bios/chandler_tyson.html|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Chandler was chosen to play for the United States team in the [[2012 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2012 London Summer Olympics]], and was named the team's starting center. The United States team finished undefeated in the tournament and won the gold medal over [[Spain national basketball team|Spain]] with a 107–100 victory. Chandler played 9 minutes, and made 1 of 2 shots from the field. He ended the game with two points, which were the first points scored during the game.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.usabasketball.com/mens/national/12_moly_game_08_stats.html |title=Gold Medal Game Statistics |publisher=usabasketball.com |date=August 12, 2012 |access-date=August 12, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120814114535/http://www.usabasketball.com/mens/national/12_moly_game_08_stats.html |archive-date=August 14, 2012  }}</ref>

==Coaching career==
In the summer of 2021, Chandler became a player development coach for the [[Dallas Mavericks]],<ref name="Mavs_October29">{{cite web |title=Tyson Chandler is - unofficially - back with the Mavs |url=https://www.mavs.com/chandlersortofback/ |access-date=October 29, 2021 |website=Dallas Mavericks|date=September 28, 2021 }}</ref> joining head coach and former teammate [[Jason Kidd]]. The strategic hire, along with former Maverick champion,  JJ Barea, was a part of the "Mavs Legends" coaching program created by owner Mark Cuban.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2021-09-29 |title=Mavs’ Jason Kidd enlists help of ex-teammate Tyson Chandler and, he hopes, the Yoda of coaches |url=https://www.dallasnews.com/sports/mavericks/2021/09/28/mavs-jason-kidd-enlists-help-of-ex-teammate-tyson-chandler-and-he-hopes-the-yoda-of-coaches/ |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=Dallas News |language=en}}</ref> Chandler, works specifically with the team's centers, including [[Dereck Lively II]]. His role is specifically geared towards helping players improve their skills and understanding of the game.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Spears |first=Marc J. |date=2023-11-03 |title=Dallas Mavericks center Dereck Lively II has a proud mentor in Tyson Chandler |url=https://andscape.com/features/dallas-mavericks-center-dereck-lively-ii-has-a-proud-mentor-in-tyson-chandler/ |access-date=2025-06-24 |website=Andscape |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Chandler's sister, Erica, played basketball at [[Pepperdine University]].<ref>[http://www.pepperdinesports.com/sports/w-baskbl/mtt/chandler_erica00.html Erica Chandler] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304054057/http://www.pepperdinesports.com/sports/w-baskbl/mtt/chandler_erica00.html |date=March 4, 2016 }}. "The man of the house: He's still only 19, but Tyson Chandler has grown up fast". ''Chicago Sun-Times''. June 23, 2002.</ref> His paternal grandmother is of [[Germans|German]] descent.<ref>{{Cite news| last = Fisher| first = Mike| title = One-on-One with Mavs center Tyson Chandler| publisher = [[Fox Sports Wisconsin]]| date = November 30, 2010| url = http://www.foxsportswisconsin.com/11/30/10/One-on-One-with-Mavs-center-Tyson-Chandl/landing.html?blockID=363592&feedID=3742| access-date = June 15, 2011}}{{Dead link|date=October 2025 |bot=InternetArchiveBot }}</ref> Chandler is the son of Frank Chandler and the late Vernie Re Threadgill.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.brightsideofthesun.com/2016/11/12/13609724/tyson-chandler-third-straight-game-phoenix-suns-brooklyn-nets-alex-len-earl-watson-nba-basketball|title=Tyson Chandler will miss third straight game|date=November 12, 2016|website=Bright Side Of The Sun}}</ref>

Chandler and his wife Kimberly were married in 2005 and separated in August 2021. In September 2021, she filed for divorce, citing irreconcilable differences. They have three children.<ref>{{cite web |author=Marconja Zor |date=September 16, 2021 |title=NBA star Tyson Chandler's wife files for divorce after 16 years |url=https://news.yahoo.com/nba-star-tyson-chandler-wife-204500799.html |accessdate=October 7, 2021 |publisher=[[Yahoo! News]]}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |date=September 17, 2021 |title=Ex-NBA Player Tyson Chandler And His Wife Are Divorcing After 16 Years |url=https://www.bet.com/article/j1uf5y/tyson-chandler-and-his-wife-are-divorcing |access-date=October 7, 2021 |publisher=[[BET]]}}</ref>

In 2013, he became an [[evangelical Christian]] and a member of [[Hillsong Church]] [[New York City|New York]].<ref> Liz Robbins, [https://www.nytimes.com/2013/02/17/nyregion/tyson-chandlers-rare-free-sundays-are-spent-with-family.html Tyson Chandler's Rare Free Sundays Are Spent With Family], nytimes.com, USA, February 17, 2013</ref>

== Off the court ==
In 2005, Tyson and Kimberly Chandler organized a charity to help [[New Orleans]] families who suffered from [[Hurricane Katrina]]. The charity helped purchase "small things" (as Chandler said) for the families' homes: TVs, stoves, microwaves, refrigerators, pots, pans etc. The wives of Chandler's teammates helped in the efforts.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Evans |first=Candy |date=June 10, 2011 |title=Houses of Dallas Mavericks emulate NBA Finals' success |url=http://www.pegasusnews.com/news/2011/jun/10/houses-dallas-mavericks-emulate-nba-finals-success/ |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110612014753/http://www.pegasusnews.com/news/2011/jun/10/houses-dallas-mavericks-emulate-nba-finals-success/ |archive-date=June 12, 2011 |access-date=June 15, 2011 |publisher=[[Pegasus News]] |df=mdy-all |quote=Tyson Chandler and his wife Kimberly are super great people — they recently organized a charity to help New Orleans families who suffered from Hurricane Katrina.}}</ref>{{better source|date=March 2026}}

In 2016, Chandler joined [[UNICEF Kid Power]] as a UNICEF Kid Power Champion for a mission in Uganda,<ref>{{Cite web |title=Tyson Chandler: UNICEF Kid Power Champion |url=https://unicefkidpower.org/champions/mission-uganda-tyson-chandler/ |url-status=usurped |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170221110915/https://unicefkidpower.org/champions/mission-uganda-tyson-chandler/ |archive-date=February 21, 2017 |website=UNICEF Kid Power}}</ref>{{better source|date=March 2026}} in an effort to fight global malnutrition and as well as raise awareness among kids, via the world's first "wearable for good".

Chandler is involved in several notable real estate investments.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Brittany |first=Natale |date=January 17, 2024 |title=Rent NBA Star Tyson Chandler’s Coastal California Mansion for $70K Per Month |url=https://www.realtor.com/news/celebrity-real-estate/tyson-chandler-newport-beach-california-mansion-is-for-rent/ |website=realtor.com}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=2015-01-27 |title=Mavs' Tyson Chandler makes $4.6 million splash in Newport Beach |url=https://www.latimes.com/socal/daily-pilot/news/la-fi-hotprop-tyson-chandler-house-20150127-story.html |access-date=2025-06-25 |website=Daily Pilot |language=en-US}}</ref> In 2012, Chandler had a successful collaboration with [[George Esquivel|Esquivel shoes]], creating a shoe he described as “hybrid boot and dress shoe.”  He also worked on a collection with [[Joseph Abboud]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Law |first=Chris |date=May 30, 2012 |title=Tyson Chandler: Knicks' Style Icon Transforming Men's Fashion |url=https://www.ebony.com/style-profile-the-knicks-tyson-chandler-409/ |access-date=2025-06-25 |website=EBONY |language=en-US}}</ref> 

In 2011, Chandler was the subject of a limited edition 100-copy [[zine]] titled "Tyson Chandler".<ref>{{Cite web |date=2011-11-21 |title=Tyson Chandler: NBA and Zine Star, Sunday Painter? |url=https://www.interviewmagazine.com/art/tyson-chandler-ari-marcopoulos |access-date=2025-06-25 |website=Interview Magazine |language=en-US}}</ref> The zine was created in fall 2011 by Camilla Venturini and the photographer [[Ari Marcopoulos]], and was the subject of a lengthy article in the ''[[Wall Street Journal]]''.<ref>{{Cite news |last=Cohen |first=Ben |date=November 19, 2011 |title=One Baller's Biggest Fan |url=https://www.wsj.com/articles/SB10001424052970203699404577046441503805050 |access-date=November 20, 2011 |publisher=Wall Street Journal}}</ref>
